verses.1: And Jehosaphat, king of Judah, returned to his house in Jerusalem in peace.
verses.2: And Yehu, son of Hanani the prophet, went before him. He said to the king, “Yehoshaphat, you should love those who are evil and hate those who hate Jehovah. In this way, you will be forgiven by Jehovah.”
verses.3: But good things were found with you, as you went through the wilderness. Prepare your heart to serve the Lord.
verses.4: And Joshua settled in Jerusalem. He led the people from Shechem to Mount Ebal. There, he brought them back to the LORD, their God.
verses.5: And judges stood in the land, in every city of Judah, in the smaller towns as well as in the larger cities.
verses.6: And he said to the judges, “See what you are doing. You do not judge according to human standards, but according to God’s laws.”
verses.7: And now, let there be fear of Jehovah over you. Observe and do as it is written: “There is no one who can stand before Jehovah our God; He takes away the sins of the people.”
verses.8: And also in Jerusalem, Joshua set up judges and priests from among the people, as well as leaders of the tribes of Israel, to judge according to the laws of God. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.9: And he commanded them, “Do this in the sight of the LORD with truth and in good faith.”
verses.10: And all disputes that come from your brothers, those who live in their cities, between laws and commandments, and between rules and judgments. Remember them carefully, and do not commit any of these things against them. Otherwise, God will be angry with you and your brothers. Do not do such things.
verses.11: And behold, Amariah, the chief priest, will tell you all the words of the LORD. And Zadok, son of Immanuel, the judge of the house of God, will also speak to you about everything related to the king and his officials. May the LORD be with you always!
